title: Tangkhul Meiphung: The Wounds of Time
title_translation: Hearthside Reflections on Time and Memory
creator: Thotdharmi Shimray
author: Thotdharmi Shimray
notes: Acclaimed contemporary poem exploring cultural memory, historical displacement, and the eternal flame of the ancestral hearth.
indigenous_tangkhul_text:
Meiphung-li pamlaga khangapik meikha theida kachikhangai,
Iramwui khararchan kacham-kacham ningli ngasungtatta.
Arārana mei-tahak sakakhung eina khon sakashung,
Chiyan-chikaning ngacheiser-haowa kha meiphung mangacheimana.

Chitharan kharuikaho eina ramwui ngashan ngacheilaka,
Wounds of time thada ning-ngalungli kashak-kakhayei shoksang.
Kha meiphungwui meira hi makhapei-mana,
Tangkhul mayarnao-wui ningli ringphang-fara!
english_translation_text:
Sitting beside the ancestral hearth, watching the glowing embers slowly breathe,
The ancient tales of our mountain land stir deep within the quiet soul.
Here our forefathers stoked the sacred fire and recounted deeds of old;
Though decades have passed and seasons shifted, the hearthstone remains unchanged.

New winds of change have swept through our valleys, altering our ways,
Leaving the wounds of time etched upon the memory of our people.
Yet the sacred flame of this ancestral hearth can never be extinguished;
It shall burn forever in the hearts of Tangkhul youth across the hills!
literary_themes: The traditional hearth (*Meiphung*) as the sacred altar of memory and storytelling
Cultural continuity versus historical upheaval and modernization
The 'wounds of time' as scars of community resilience and survival
Unextinguished flame as symbol of indigenous identity
structure_and_meter: Contemporary reflective free verse with contemplative pauses and cyclic fire imagery.
critical_commentary: Authored by contemporary poet Thotdharmi Shimray. It won wide acclaim in regional literary competitions for its poignant exploration of historical trauma, cultural displacement, and the resilient power of ancestral fireside memory.

poetic_vocabulary_terms.Meiphung: The traditional three-stone village hearth, center of family fellowship and oral lore
poetic_vocabulary_terms.Meikha: Glowing coals / living warmth preserved overnight beneath ash
poetic_vocabulary_terms.Mei-tahak: To kindle and feed the ancestral fire with seasoned pine wood
poetic_vocabulary_terms.Ning-ngalung: The innermost chamber of the heart and consciousness
